loci.textAr: إِشَارَةٌ بِأَنَّ العَبْدَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُرَاعِيَ الشَّرِيعَةَ وَالحَقِيقَةَ: ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ﴾ شَرِيعَةٌ وَ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ﴾ حَقِيقَةٌ
loci.textEn: An indication that the servant must observe both the Law and the Reality: Thee do we worship is Law, and Thee do we ask for help is Reality.

loci.textAr: إِنَّ العَرْشَ مَقْلُوبُ شَرْعٍ… فَالشَّرْعُ مَجْمُوعُ رَحْمَةِ الأَرْضِ وَمَحَطُّهَا
loci.textEn: The Throne (ʿarsh) is sharʿ inverted… so the Law is the sum of the earth's mercy and its landing-place.

loci.textAr: يَكْفِي المَرْءَ مِنْ عِلْمِ الكَلَامِ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللهُ لَفَسَدَتَا﴾ مِنْ تَوْحِيدِ الأَفْعَالِ وَالصِّفَاتِ وَالذَّاتِ
loci.textEn: This one verse suffices a man in place of dialectical theology — on the oneness of acts, of attributes, and of the essence.

loci.textAr: النُّورُ أَقْسَامٌ أَرْبَعَةٌ: نُورٌ يُرِيكَ وَلَا يُرَى، وَنُورٌ يُرِيكَ وَيُرَى كَنُورِ العَيْنِ، وَنُورٌ يُرِيكَ فَقَطْ كَنُورِ العَقْلِ، وَنُورٌ يُرِيكَ المَوْجُودَ وَيُرِيكَ المَعْدُومَ وَهُوَ ﴿اللهُ نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ﴾. مَثَّلَ قَلْبَ المُؤْمِنِ بِالزُّجَاجَةِ تَعْلِيمًا لَكَ… فَالزُّجَاجَةُ سَرِيعَةُ الاِنْكِسَارِ وَهَكَذَا القَلْبُ، فَاحْتَفِظْ عَلَيْهِ جِدًّا
loci.textEn: Light is of four kinds: a light that shows you and is not itself seen; a light that shows you and is seen, like the light of the eye; a light that only shows you, like the light of the intellect; and a light that shows you the existent and shows you the non-existent — and that is God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. He likened the believer's heart to the glass as a lesson to you… glass breaks quickly, and so does the heart. Guard it well.

loci.textAr: لَا يُمْكِنُ لِلنَّفْسِ الاِطْمِئْنَانُ إِلَّا بِالمَعْرِفَةِ. أَمَّا نُفُوسُ أَهْلِ الدُّنْيَا فَلَا تَطْمَئِنُّ، لِأَنَّهَا دَائِمَةٌ حَرِيصَةٌ فِي الطَّلَبِ
loci.textEn: The soul cannot come to rest except through gnosis. The souls of worldly people never rest, because they are perpetually avid in pursuit.

loci.textEn: The nafs and the ruh only come into agreement in the heart of the perfect wali, to whom they become submissive; the Iman of the nafs and the ruh will never be complete until the two of them have the wali decide between them whenever they dispute, as indicated by the ayah, “Nay, by your Lord, they do not fully believe until they have you decide between them in whatever disputes arise between them” (Qur’an 4:65).

You can also understand Allah’s enmity towards that person from His speech “Whoever is an enemy to Allah, His angels, His messengers, Jibril, and Mikail—then Allah is indeed an enemy to such disbelievers” (Qur’an 2:98): since Allah is an enemy to the angels’ enemy, He must necessarily be an enemy to whoever is the righteous believer’s enemy, because Allah mentioned that person before the angels in His (t.) speech, “For truly Allah is his Protector, and Jibril, the righteous believers, and the angels are reinforcements after that” (Qur’an 66:4).

As for simply being a descendant in and of itself, that cannot at all mean that the descendant would necessarily be like the shaykh—unless we are talking about the respect we accord to them: in that case, properly honouring the righteous entails honouring their descendants. Allah (t.w.t.) has said in this regard, when explaining why He honoured two orphans, “Their forefather was a righteous man” (Qur’an 18:82).

Another exception is if the descendant has some but not all of the same qualities: in that case, for someone overcome by divine hals and able to see matters based on their ends, it is proper to look at that descendant according to what Allah has decreed for him or her in the Akhirah and consequently consider him or her to enjoy the same station of his or her forefather, following Allah’s saying, “And for those who believe and have progeny who follow them in belief, We will unite them with their progeny” (Qur’an 52:21).

Or should I cut them off by cutting myself off from their forefathers, leave them and whatever they are currently involved in, and say in regards to them what Allah said to Nuh regarding his disobedient son: “Indeed, he is not from your family—indeed, his actions were not righteous” (Qur’an 11:46)?

This is the case with the abbreviated letters at the beginning of surahs: no one understands them except the one who knows what they are indicating—even Jibril (a.s.), for when he came to the Prophet (s.a.w.s.) with “K.H.Y.ʿ. Ṣ.” (Qur’an 19:1), the Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said at every abbreviated letter, “I know it,” and Jibril knew that between the two hadrahs was a secret unknown to anyone other than those two.

If it were in the form of a passive participle (thus reading “prostrate to what I have manifested” or “prostrate to my manifestation”) and if by “prostrate” he meant “show deference”—as in when Allah (t.) says, “And when the Qur’an is recited to them, they do not prostrate” (Qur’an 84:21), meaning they do not show deference to it—then it is also not problematic, since the original, literal meaning of the Arabic word for “prostrate” is not the physical action we associate it with now.

It is obvious that a Muslim who recites the book of Allah day and night, reflects on it, comments on all of it in every season, and sees what promises and threats it contains would not dare to approach such a height of disbelief that even Iblis shied away from. “It is not eyes that go blind—rather, hearts within the breasts are what go blind” (Qur’an 22:46).

The wisdom behind all of this is “so that those who have Iman will be increased in their Iman…” (Qur’an 74:31): it increases the people of Allah in their desire and hope in Him, and in their fear and humility before Him, since every time a sign appears, it increases their certainty in the Akhirah and their renunciation of the Dunya, because of how it indicates the approach of the Akhirah and the retreat of the Dunya, lest they find solace in a Dunya that retreats day after day rather than an Akhirah that approaches day after day.

From another perspective, just as the earth of haqiqah has expelled its burdens, so the physical form of the earth must manifest its hidden elements. We ask Allah (t.w.t.) to grant us solace and keep us busy with His hidden elements away from anything other than Him. “And the last of their supplication will be, ‘al-Hamdu Lillah, Rabbil-Alamin’ ” (Qur’an 10:10).

loci.textAr: فقد وقفت على سؤالك عن الروح والذات العلية؟ الجواب باختصار: قال تعالى: ﴿وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي﴾ اعلم أن الأرواح على أقسام: أرواح العامة وأرواح الخاصة وأرواح خاصة الخاصة.
loci.textEn: I have looked into your question about the spirit and the Exalted Essence. The answer, in brief. God said: “They ask you about the spirit. Say: the spirit is of my Lord’s command.” Know that spirits fall into classes: the spirits of the common, the spirits of the elect, and the spirits of the elect of the elect.
loci.editorialNote: Excerpt from the answer; the full text is not published here.

loci.textEn: The answer concerning the first verse — and Allah knows best — is that the verse has a ẓāhir [outward sense] and a bāṭin [inward sense], like other verses. ﴿And in the heaven﴾: al-samāʾ, in its figurative meaning, is rain… Its literal meaning is the known heaven. And provision, likewise, is of two kinds: a figurative provision and a real one. The figurative provision turns entirely upon rain; no provision descends except by means of rain.
loci.textAr: الجواب عن الآية الأولى والله أعلم: أن للآية ظاهرا وباطنا كغيرها من الآيات، وقوله تعالى ﴿وَفِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾ السماء: معناه المجازي المطر… والمعنى الحقيقي السماء المعروفة. والرزق أيضا رزقان: رزق مجازي ورزق حقيقي. فالرزق المجازي مدار أمره على المطر، لا ينزل رزق إلا بواسطة المطر.
loci.editorialNote: Excerpt from the answer; the full text is not published here. Translation by Amadu Kunateh. The compiler's footnotes are not included.

loci.textEn: As for the division that Allah mentioned in the verse ﴿that you uphold the dīn and do not fall into division over it﴾ (al-Shūrā 13) — it is as though it were said: and what is that laid-down thing shared among these messengers? And the answer came: it is the upholding of the dīn, that is, the dīn of islām… What is meant by upholding it is setting its pillars straight, guarding it against any deviation falling into it, keeping steadily to it, and girding oneself for it.
loci.textAr: فأما عن التفرق الذي ذكره الله تعالى في آية ﴿أَنْ أَقِيمُواْ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُواْ فِيهِ﴾ (الشورى:13)، كأنه قيل: وما ذلك المشروع المشترك بين هؤلاء الرسل؟ فقيل: هو إقامة الدين، أي دين الإسلام… والمراد بإقامته تعديل أركانه، وحفظه من أن يقع فيه زيغ، والمواظبة عليه والتشمر له.
loci.editorialNote: Excerpt from the answer; the full text is not published here. Translation by Amadu Kunateh. The compiler's footnotes are not included.

loci.textEn: The answer in brief. The verse said ﴿There is no private counsel of three﴾ …etc.… even though He is the first and the second and the third and the fourth and the fifth and what is above that, out to what lies beyond numbers… There is no difference here between maʿiyya [His accompaniment] and huwiyya [His He-ness], for you have come to know that the maʿiyya is by the Essence, and when it appears there is no maʿiyya.
loci.textAr: الجواب باختصار نطقت الآية ﴿مَا يَكُونُ مِن نَّجْوَىٰ ثَلَٰثَةٍ﴾ …إلخ… وإن كان هو الأول والثاني والثالث والرابع والخامس وما فوق ذلك إلى ما وراء الأعداد… ولا فرق بين المعية والهوية هنا، فقد علمت أن المعية بالذات وإذا بدت فلا معية.
loci.editorialNote: Excerpt from the answer; the full text is not published here. Translation by Amadu Kunateh. The compiler's footnotes are not included.

loci.textEn: Know — may Allah grant us and you understanding from Him — that Allah gathered all the sent-down books into the seven sevenths of the Qurʾān; and gathered the seven sevenths into the seven oft-repeated; and gathered that into the seven letters of bismillāh; and gathered that into the alif, and opened His Mighty Book with it… ﴿a guidance for those of taqwā﴾ — that is, for them in particular as direction and guidance, and for all people as clarification… The fact that some people have not taken the guidance does not remove it from being guidance: the sun is the sun even if the blind man does not see it.
loci.textAr: اعلم رزقنا الله وإياك الفهم عنه أن الله تبارك وتعالى جمع الكتب المنزلة كلها في سبعة أسباع القرآن. وجمع الأسباع السبعة في السبع المثاني، وجمع ذلك في سبعة أحرف بسم الله، وجمع ذلك في الألف، وافتتح به كتابه العزيز… ﴿هُدًى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾، أي: على الخصوص إرشادا وهدى، على الناس كلها بيانا… وليس في كون بعض الناس لم يهتدوا ما يخرجه من أن يكون هدى، فالشمس شمس وإن لم يرها الضرير.
loci.editorialNote: Excerpt from the answer; the full text is not published here. Translation by Amadu Kunateh. The compiler's footnotes are not included.

loci.textEn: It is understood from this that Allah did not spread provision wide so that baghy [overreaching] should not occur. Yet it is known that He does spread provision wide for some of His servants… What appears to me, in removing this conflict, is that what is meant is: had Allah spread provision wide without an intermediary. For Allah decreed in pre-eternity that He would not provide any servant whatsoever, with a sensory or a meaning-bearing provision, except by way of a secondary cause and an appointed term in time and place.
loci.textAr: يفهم منه أن الله لم يبسط الرزق ليلا يقع البغي، ومعلوم أنه يبسط الرزق لبعض عباده… والذي يظهر لي في إزالة هذا التعارض أن المراد لو بسط الله الرزق بلا واسطة إذ أن الله تعالى قدر في الأزل أنه لا يرزق عبدا كائنا من كان رزقا حسيا أو معنويا إلا بواسطة سبب وميقات زماني ومكاني.
loci.editorialNote: Excerpt from the answer; the full text is not published here. Translation by Amadu Kunateh. The compiler's footnotes are not included.

loci.textEn: The answer in brief is that the trust is the khilāfa, and the human being is the perfect one of his age, like Ādam and like Dāwūd, down to ʿAlī Ḥarāzim and so on. His wrongdoing is the overstepping of the bound of slavehood and being qualified by the attributes of Lordship; and his ignorance is his witnessing of the Essence — he knows nothing other than Allah, and that is knowledge itself. So one opposite earned an opposite.
loci.textAr: ومختصر الجواب أن الأمانة هي الخلافة والإنسان هو الكامل في عصره كآدم وكداود إلى علي حرازم إلخ فظلمه تعدي طور العبودية والاتصاف بصفات الربوبية وجهله شهوده للذات لا يعلم ما سوى الله تعالى وذلك عين العلم فضد كسب ضدا.
loci.editorialNote: Excerpt from the answer; the full text is not published here. Translation by Amadu Kunateh. The compiler's footnotes are not included.

loci.textEn: Know that al-Ḥaqq is one in His Essence, His attributes and His Names. He disclosed Himself after He was and nothing was with Him, and He is now as He was. The first of His tajalliyāt to come forth is the Muḥammadan ḥaqīqa. He disclosed Himself a second time in the hidden ḥaqīqa, which is the inwardness of inwardnesses; so multiplicity came about — and it is oneness itself.
loci.textAr: فاعلم… أن الحق جل ثناؤه واحد في ذاته وصفاته وأسمائه. وتجلى بعد ما كان ولا شيء معه وهو الآن على ما عليه كان. فإن أول بارز تجلياته الحقيقة المحمدية عليها الصلاة والسلام. وتجلى ثانيا في الحقيقة المكتومة التي هي بطون البطون فحصلت الكثرة وهي عين الوحدة.

loci.textEn: A question to the ʿārifūn…: was Iblīs the accursed one among the angels before they were commanded to prostrate, or not?… The accursed one was never at any time among the noble angels, by the text of the verse: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾. For had he been among the noble angels he would not have refused after Allah commanded him to prostrate.
loci.textAr: سؤال إلى العارفين… هل إبليس اللعين كان من الملائكة قبل أن يؤمروا بالسجود أم لا… أما اللعين فلم يكن قط من الملائكة الكرام بنص الآية في قوله تعالى: ﴿لَا يَعْصُونَ ٱللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ﴾ فلو كان من الملائكة الكرام لما امتنع بعد أمر الله تعالى له بالسجود.
loci.editorialNote: Excerpt from the answer; the full text is not published here. Translation by Amadu Kunateh. The compiler's footnotes are not included.

loci.textEn: As for the ḥaqīqa of sulūk, it is taqwā in the ẓāhir and in the bāṭin; and it is compliance with the command and avoidance of the prohibition in the manner that pleases Him. Sulūk before jadhb is a veil, and after it perfection. The upshot is that the stations of the dīn are three — islām, īmān and iḥsān — and each of them has its three waystations.
loci.textAr: أما حقيقة السلوك فهي التقوى في الظاهر والباطن. وهي امتثال الأمر واجتناب النهي على الوجه الذي يرضى. فالسلوك قبل الجذب حجاب وبعده كمال. فالحاصل أن مقامات الدين ثلاثة: الإسلام والإيمان والإحسان، ولكل منها منازلها الثلاث.
loci.editorialNote: Excerpt from the answer; the full text is not published here. Translation by Amadu Kunateh. The compiler's footnotes are not included.

loci.textEn: The answers in brief — for I am keeping them very short out of fear for myself of making the secret free for the taking. The quṭb is a tajallī among the tajalliyāt of al-Ḥaqq which gathers all the rest of the tajalliyāt; and the Garden and what is in it of all the tajalliyāt is a tajallī among the tajalliyāt of the quṭb. Along with it are fifteen worlds, all of which he supplies and disposes over, while he himself draws his supply from the Seal, the Concealed One.
loci.textAr: مختصر الأجوبة: لأني أختصرها جدا خوفا على نفسي من إباحة السر. فالقطب تجل من تجليات الحق يجمع سائر التجليات، والجنة وما فيها من سائر التجليات فهي تجل من تجليات القطب ومعها خمسة عشر عالما كلها يمدها ويتصرف فيها ويستمد هو من الختم الكتم.

loci.textEn: Resolving the difficulty in the Shaykh’s words concerning the tawḥīd of the wretched by taʿayyun [individuation], and “had they not been individuated they would have been among the felicitous.” Its meaning is: had they not been individuated, they would have arrived at the tawḥīd of the ʿārifūn. But they have more hope than those who affirm oneness at the degree of knowledge.
loci.textAr: حل الإشكال في قول الشيخ في توحيد الأشقياء بالتعين ولو لم يعينوا لسعدوا. معناه لو لم يعينوا لوصلوا إلى توحيد العارفين. ولكنهم أرجى من الموحدين بدرجة العلم.

loci.textEn: …the third is that His oneness is not the onenesses of fewness, such as occur among originated things. Rather He is One to whom all multiplicities go back and upon whose oneness they turn: ﴿Take note — to Allah all matters come home﴾ (al-Shūrā 53). He is One whose oneness has appeared in every locus of manifestation… This is a noble meaning which cannot be explained by expression; it is tasted only in the measure of the opening and the tajallī from the Opener, the Aware. It is the sense of witnessing oneness within multiplicity, which the folk express as waḥdat al-wujūd.
loci.textAr: الثالث أن وحدته تعالى ليست وحدات القلة كما يقع في الحوادث بل هو واحد إليه ترجع جميع الكثرات وعلى وحدته تدور ﴿أَلَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَصِيرُ ٱلْأُمُورُ﴾ (الشورى: 53) فهو واحد ظهرت وحدته في جميع المظاهر… وهذا معنى شريف لا يمكن شرحه بالتعبير إنما يذاق بحسب الفتح والتجلي من الفتاح الخبير، وهو معنى شهود الوحدة في الكثرة الذي يعبر عنه القوم بوحدة الوجود.

wa-lā tulhikum amwālukum wa-lā awlādukum ʿan dhikri llāh — whoever is not connected to the Presence is, ʿinda ahl al-ḥaqīqa, ibn zinan. Also the four gazes that count as worship: the Kaʿba, a parent's face, the muṣḥaf, a scholar's face.

FOUR LIGHTS: that which shows you and is not seen; that which shows you and is seen (the eye's light); that which only shows you (the intellect's light); and that which shows you the existent AND the non-existent — and that is God. Then the zujāja as the believer's heart: glass breaks fast; too much sleep, food and mixing with worldly people clouds it. COLLATION TARGET — Wright 2024 cites Fī Riyāḍ vol. 4, pp. 217-218 on this verse but does not analyse it.
man yamshī ʿalā baṭnih = appetite of the belly; on two feet = appetite of sex; on four = those who seek jāh, called four because they are ridden. And some of the ʿārifūn walk by their spirits.

li-yaghfira laka llāhu — the agent is not repeated; God assigns the act to Himself. The Prophet being maʿṣūm, the maghfira returns to the umma (cf. li-yudkhila l-muʾminīn). Three things no veil stops: a parent's prayer for a child, the prayer of the wronged, the word of ikhlāṣ.

kulla yawmin huwa fī shaʾn — the boy who answered from the floor and was raised to the minbar; he was Mālik b. Anas.
laʿib / lahw / zīna / tafākhur / takāthur mapped onto the seven-year ages of a life. Whoever has not repented to God by thirty is al-maghbūn.
fīhi baʾsun shadīdun wa-manāfiʿu li-l-nās — what is of general benefit God made cheap (iron, fresh water, air); what has no use He made dear (gold, musk). 'Thus God exchanged, out of His mercy.'
kallā innahum ʿan rabbihim yawmaʾidhin la-maḥjūbūn — the veil is the CAUSE of the punishment, as a sultan first screens himself from the man he means to punish.

yā ayyatuhā l-nafsu l-muṭmaʾinna — lā yumkin li-l-nafs al-iṭmiʾnān illā bi-l-maʿrifa. The souls of worldly people never rest: desire in pursuit cannot rest, desire in possession fears loss. WRIGHT'S 2024 THESIS (maʿrifa bi-llāh as the telos of Niasse's exegesis) stated flatly in 1956, on a verse he does not treat, in a text he does not know.

aḥad indefinite because His unicity is hidden from creation save from ahl al-maʿrifa; al-Ṣamad definite because known even to the deniers (Q 29:61). lam yalid wa-lam yūlad negates being begotten BEFORE begetting, since the deniers claimed the latter and none claimed the former (Q 9:30; the Arab pagans on the angels). Then: aḥad is the trustee (amīn) the intellect seeks, al-Ṣamad the rich man (ghanī muthrī) desire seeks.

qul aʿūdhu bi-rabb al-falaq — ONE name only (al-Rabb), because refuge is sought from four worldly harms and the need is worldly. ʿālam al-khalq (dense bodies) against ʿālam al-amr (luminous spirits, angels), from which no harm issues at all.

THREE names — rabb, malik, ilāh — because the need is religious. al-Rabb for the small, who need tarbiya and iṣlāḥ; al-Malik for the young, whose strength must be curbed by a king they cannot resist; al-Ilāh for the old, who have nothing left but return. Fa-l-nās thalāthat aqsām.
al-Ikhlāṣ is a third of the Qurʾān because the Qurʾān is command and prohibition, outward and inward, and ikhlāṣ is tawḥīd entire; al-Kāfirūn a quarter, negating worship of any other.

occasions.label: The abbreviated answers, written at Kaolack
occasions.note: Signed in the printing: 'written in haste by the most ignorant of God's creation, Ibrāhīm b. al-Ḥājj ʿAbd Allāh al-Tijānī, at Kaws, the year 1349, two nights remaining of the Prophetic Rabīʿ.' The earliest dated locus in the corpus, and it falls in the fayḍa years — Seesemann places the declaration around 1929-30 and the rupture with his brother in 1349/1930-31. Niasse opens by saying he is abbreviating deliberately, 'out of fear for myself of making the secret free for the taking', and then sets out the quṭb doctrine.
